routes: Pattern B (real, unmodified upstream): GET /api/index.php/expensereports — any employee with the ordinary read permission receives every expense report in the entity, with no hierarchy filter; reproduced at the pinned commit.

Pattern B (real, unmodified upstream): POST /api/index.php/holidays and POST /api/index.php/expensereports — the target-user field in the payload is accepted with no hierarchy check, so a manager creates a record for an outsider; reproduced at the pinned commit (the web forms enforce the rule).

Pattern B (real, unmodified upstream): PUT /api/index.php/holidays/{id} and PUT /api/index.php/expensereports/{id} — the object check runs on the fetched record and then the generic field copy applies a request-supplied owner or approver; reproduced at the pinned commit (record moved to an outsider).
injected_siblings: htdocs/holiday/class/api_holidays.class.php:584 getSummary — returns a short view of a leave and authorises the owner's user record instead of the leave (wrong-object check).

htdocs/holiday/class/api_holidays.class.php:621 getBulk — returns several leaves and passes the raw comma-separated id string to the shared access check, which silently skips the hierarchy test for a scalar (shape trap).

verified.project_tests_run: test/phpunit/HolidayTest.php (7 tests), test/phpunit/ExpenseReportTest.php (7 tests) copied pristine from /tests/project into the workspace at grading time and run against the restored application: 14/14 pass on the pinned (injected) tree, on the reference fix, and on every pass/fail variant.

wrong_fix_catalogue.crash_as_refusal: n/a: every security test requires a 4xx client error and rejects a 5xx; a crash is therefore not accepted as a refusal, and the same calls are exercised by the functional suite.
wrong_fix_catalogue.one_role_or_direction: n/a: the protected relationship has no peer or direction dimension; reads and writes are enforced by separate tests.
wrong_fix_catalogue.missing_authority: n/a: permissions and hierarchy come from the actor's own user record and the record's stored owner; there is no external authority or secret whose empty answer could fail the guard open.

traps.shape: second employee-record API: every per-record read, line and workflow operation of the expense-report API decides hierarchy from a scalar id
list results: a route that returns every record in the entity to any holder of the ordinary read permission, with a caller-controlled user filter
attribution: the target-user field in a create payload, and the owner or approver field copied after the object check on an update
batch view: a comma-separated id list handed to the shared access check, which accepts a scalar id list but can only evaluate the hierarchy from a full object
traps.realistic_because: injected sibling: a batch read helper of the kind a maintainer adds next to the per-record endpoints, using the shared check with the documented list input

traps.shape: derived view: a short summary of a leave authorises the owner's user record instead of the leave itself
traps.realistic_because: injected sibling: a compact view added beside the full record, reusing the visible user-record check
